title: Collaborative design as a form of professional development
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether and how collaborative design of curriculum and learning materials can function as professional development for teachers. The authors argue that many teacher design activities are grounded in situated learning and cultural-historical activity theory, and that key features of productive teacher learning include situatedness, agency, and the cyclical nature of learning and educational change.

Rather than testing a single intervention in one setting, the paper synthesizes three case descriptions from different contexts: an online participatory professional development model for secondary English teachers in the United States; teacher design teams working on curriculum reform in Ethiopia, Ghana, and Tanzania; and the Remote Networked School initiative in Quebec, Canada. Across these cases, teachers collaboratively designed, adapted, enacted, and revised curricular materials, often with support from researchers, facilitators, or domain experts, and in some cases with technology-mediated collaboration.

The main conclusion is that collaborative design can support teacher learning when it is authentic to teachers’ work, well scaffolded, and organized as an iterative cycle of design, implementation, reflection, and revision. The paper emphasizes that teachers learn not only through exposure to new ideas but also through active participation in designing materials for their own contexts, negotiating shared problems, and observing the effects of their designs in practice. It also highlights that successful implementation depends on supportive partnerships, access to expertise, and alignment with local needs and constraints.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed conceptual/theoretical synthesis with three qualitative case descriptions of collaborative design as professional development, not an experimental evaluation of a technology intervention. The paper uses design-based research and case evidence, but it does not report causal impact estimates for a specific AI or instructional technology.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has clear educational relevance for understanding collaborative curriculum design and teacher learning, but it does not demonstrate measurable student or system impact from a technology intervention. Any implications are indirect and theoretical rather than quantified.
